title: PD-MT245-ProseDiffParityAndPerfProofs

scope.summary:
GOAL: Author and run the proof suite that (a) PROVES the native prose diff/merge (MT-241) is behaviourally equivalent to the React reference app/src/lib/editor/document_diff_merge.ts BEFORE that file is deleted, (b) enforces performance budgets on large prose documents, and (c) fuzzes the engine for panics and merge-plan totality. This MT is the GATE that lets the TR family remove the TS reference: it EXPLICITLY BLOCKS TR MT-261 (lifecycle.blocks = ['MT-261']) — the parity fixtures MUST be captured and green while document_diff_merge.ts still exists, because once it is deleted the equivalence can never be re-derived.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: Flat proof files under src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/ : (a) tests/prose_diff_proof/parity_fixtures.json — the equivalence corpus (input doc triples + the EXPECTED block statuses and merge-plan classifications, captured from the TS reference); (b) tests/test_prose_diff_parity.rs — feeds each fixture through MT-241 and asserts native output equals the recorded TS output; (c) tests/test_prose_diff_perf.rs — the large-document latency budgets; (d) tests/test_prose_diff_fuzz.rs — random-edit no-panic + merge-plan totality; (e) tests/prose_diff_proof/perf_manifest.json — machine-readable per-scenario budget/measured/status. NO product-code edits (proof-only), NO backend, NO change to MT-241/242/243.

PART A — PARITY vs the TS reference (the removal gate):
  A1. Capture the reference outputs WHILE document_diff_merge.ts EXISTS. For each fixture (a set spanning: identical docs; pure add; pure remove; single modify; multi-block modify; a moved block; interleaved add/remove/modify; a code-block (monacoCodeBlock) edit; nested-content blocks; empty doc vs non-empty; and the 3-way cases: local-only, remote-only, both-same, conflict, and no-change-skip), record the EXPECTED buildRichDocumentDiff block statuses (unchanged|modified|added|removed) and planRichDocumentMerge classifications (local_only|remote_only|both_same|conflict, with the correct set of emitted blocks) into parity_fixtures.json. Prefer generating these from the actual TS (a small node/ts-node harness run against document_diff_merge.ts, committed as the capture method) over hand-transcription; if the TS harness cannot run in the environment, hand-transcribe from a direct read of the file and record NOT_RUN_FROM_TS_WITH_REASON in the manifest — never fabricate a passing capture.
  A2. tests/test_prose_diff_parity.rs feeds each fixture's input triple through MT-241 (ProseDiffEngine::diff and BlockMergeEngine::three_way) and asserts native block statuses + merge classifications EQUAL the recorded reference values. Fixtures are chosen in the parity-neutral regime of MT-241 (id-free, no cross-gap move) EXCEPT the dedicated move fixture, which asserts the DOCUMENTED native superset behaviour (a note in the fixture marks it native-enhanced, not a TS-divergence bug).
  A3. A tripwire test asserts document_diff_merge.ts still exists at author time (so the gate is meaningful) and records its path; when TR MT-261 removes it, this suite must already be GREEN and frozen as the parity record.

PART B — PERFORMANCE budgets (env-overridable, MT-045 PERF_BUDGET_* pattern):
  B1. Diff a 1000-block document against an edited copy (deterministic seeded generation, in-process, no backend): budget <= 100 ms for ProseDiffEngine::diff. Env override PROSE_PERF_BUDGET_DIFF_MS.
  B2. Three-way plan over a 1000-block base/local/remote triple: budget <= 200 ms for BlockMergeEngine::three_way. Env override PROSE_PERF_BUDGET_MERGE_MS.
  B3. Separate fixture GENERATION (not timed) from the measured operation via std::time::Instant placed AFTER all setup (MT-045 CTRL-2). Record measured values + PASS/FAIL to perf_manifest.json written atomically (temp-file + rename). Budgets overridable so a slow host widens without code change; record the MEASURED value, not just PASS.

PART C — FUZZ:
  C1. Random block edits (seeded RNG so failures reproduce): generate a base doc, apply N random block operations (insert/delete/edit/move) to produce local and remote, run diff + three_way + apply; assert NO panic across many iterations.
  C2. Merge-plan TOTALITY: assert every block index is accounted for — every changed block appears in exactly one plan classification and applying the plan (with an arbitrary but complete conflict resolution) yields a document whose block count and content are consistent with the chosen sides (no block silently dropped or duplicated). This is the block-level analogue of the code-merge tiling invariant.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read app/src/lib/editor/document_diff_merge.ts IN FULL (the parity target) and MT-241 prose_diff.rs (ProseDiffEngine/BlockMergeEngine/BlockMergePlan/ProseDiffStatus/BlockMergeStatus/MergeChoice/ProseMergeError) and MT-045 (tests/perf_proof/*: the PERF_BUDGET_* override pattern, atomic manifest write via temp+rename, fixture-vs-measured separation, seeded deterministic generators) as the proof-authoring precedent.
2. Build the capture harness (node/ts-node against document_diff_merge.ts) OR the documented hand-transcription; write parity_fixtures.json with input triples + expected outputs + a capture-method field per fixture.
3. Author test_prose_diff_parity.rs (equivalence), test_prose_diff_perf.rs (B1/B2 with env overrides + manifest write), test_prose_diff_fuzz.rs (C1 no-panic + C2 totality) using seeded generators.
4. Register the three test files under [[test]] in src/frontend/handshake_native/Cargo.toml if the harness requires explicit registration (proof-only Cargo.toml edit allowed, MT-045 precedent).
5. Run: parity green, perf within budgets (or env-widened with the measured value recorded), fuzz no-panic + totality. Write perf_manifest.json atomically. Record the document_diff_merge.ts existence tripwire.
6. Confirm lifecycle.blocks=['MT-261'] is honoured operationally: the TR removal MT must not proceed until this suite is green; state that dependency in the proof output.
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (document_diff_merge.ts is READ as the parity target and its existence asserted; it is NOT edited here — its removal is TR MT-261..264)
src/backend/** (no backend; the prose diff/merge is pure client-side)
src/frontend/handshake_native/src/** (proof-only MT; no product-code edits — MT-241/242/243 own the product code)
acceptance_criteria: parity_fixtures.json exists with input doc triples plus recorded EXPECTED buildRichDocumentDiff block statuses and planRichDocumentMerge classifications, each fixture tagged with its capture method (from-TS-harness or hand-transcribed-with-reason); no fabricated captures.

test_prose_diff_parity.rs feeds every fixture through MT-241 and asserts native block statuses + merge-plan classifications EQUAL the recorded reference; the suite is GREEN while document_diff_merge.ts still exists.
A tripwire asserts document_diff_merge.ts exists at author time and records its path, making the removal gate meaningful; the parity suite is the frozen equivalence record TR MT-261 relies on.

test_prose_diff_perf.rs proves a 1000-block diff <= 100 ms (PROSE_PERF_BUDGET_DIFF_MS override) and a 1000-block three-way plan <= 200 ms (PROSE_PERF_BUDGET_MERGE_MS override), with fixture generation excluded from the measured span and measured values recorded.

test_prose_diff_fuzz.rs runs seeded random block edits over many iterations with NO panic across diff/three_way/apply, and asserts merge-plan totality (every changed block classified exactly once; apply drops/duplicates no block).

perf_manifest.json is written atomically (temp-file + rename) with per-scenario {id, budget, measured_value, unit, status}; a passing run has 0 FAIL (or env-widened budgets with the real measured value recorded, never a hidden widening).
Proof-only: no edits under src/frontend/handshake_native/src/** or src/backend/** (grep/lineage-provable); only tests/** and a proof-scope Cargo.toml change.
The suite explicitly documents that it BLOCKS TR MT-261 (lifecycle.blocks) and that the TR removal must not proceed until this suite is green.

cargo test -p handshake-native prose_diff_fuzz -- --nocapture 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed'
test -f app/src/lib/editor/document_diff_merge.ts && echo TS_REFERENCE_PRESENT (parity gate meaningful)

python -c "import json,sys; m=json.load(open('src/frontend/handshake_native/tests/prose_diff_proof/perf_manifest.json')); f=[e for e in m if e['status']=='FAIL']; print('FAIL:',len(f)); assert len(f)==0"
expected_tests: parity: every fixture's native diff block statuses equal the recorded TS statuses
parity: every fixture's native three-way classifications equal the recorded TS classifications (including no-change-skip)
parity: document_diff_merge.ts existence tripwire (gate is meaningful)
perf: 1000-block diff <= 100 ms (env-overridable), measured value recorded
perf: 1000-block three-way plan <= 200 ms (env-overridable), measured value recorded
fuzz: N seeded random-edit iterations never panic across diff/three_way/apply
fuzz: merge-plan totality — every changed block classified once; apply drops/duplicates no block
implementation_notes: This suite is the REMOVAL GATE for the TS reference: lifecycle.blocks=['MT-261']. document_diff_merge.ts is DELETED by TR MT-261..264; the equivalence CANNOT be re-derived after deletion, so the fixtures must be captured and green now. Do not defer any part of Part A.

Prefer capturing expected outputs from the ACTUAL TS (a committed node/ts-node harness against document_diff_merge.ts) so the parity record is real; if the TS harness cannot run, hand-transcribe from a direct read and record NOT_RUN_FROM_TS_WITH_REASON per fixture — never fabricate a passing capture (GLOBAL-TRUTH).

Reuse the MT-045 proof precedent verified 2026-07-21: PERF_BUDGET_* env overrides for every budget, Instant placed AFTER setup so generation is never timed, atomic manifest write (temp-file + rename), seeded deterministic generators so failures reproduce, and recording the MEASURED value not just PASS.

The parity fixtures live in MT-241's parity-neutral regime (id-free, no cross-gap move) so native==TS, EXCEPT one dedicated move fixture that asserts MT-241's documented superset (stable-id/similarity) behaviour and is tagged native-enhanced — proving the hardening is intentional, not a parity break.

Merge-plan totality is the block-level analogue of the code diff tiling invariant (code_editor/diff_engine.rs diff_blocks_tile_both_buffers_without_gaps): every changed block is classified exactly once and apply neither drops nor duplicates a block.
Cross-family seams (reference only): MT-241 engine (under test), MT-242/243 UI (not under test here), TR MT-261 removal gate (blocked by this MT).

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Proof-only MT (parity/perf/fuzz test suite over the pure MT-241 engine); it renders no operator surface.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Test/proof suite with no operator-visible behaviour; UserManual coverage of the prose diff/merge lands with MT-242 and MT-243.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations: FlightRecorder: NOT_APPLICABLE-with-reason — synchronous in-process test suite; it emits no product runtime events.

internal_diagnostics: WIRED — perf_manifest.json + per-fixture capture-method records + the TS-existence tripwire make every parity/perf/fuzz result machine-readable and reproducible by a no-context model.
Palmistry: NOT_APPLICABLE-with-reason — no long-running child process; bounded in-process test run.
risk_if_missed: The TS reference document_diff_merge.ts is removed by TR MT-261..264 with NO frozen equivalence record, so any future divergence of the native prose diff/merge from the intended behaviour is undetectable; large-document diff/merge could regress into unbounded latency; and a fuzzing gap lets a malformed block sequence panic or silently drop blocks during a real merge, corrupting a document.

risks: RISK-1: The parity fixtures are captured AFTER document_diff_merge.ts is removed (or fabricated), so the 'equivalence' proves nothing and the removal gate is hollow.
RISK-2: Perf budgets are set for a fast dev host and always fail (or are silently widened by an env override) on slow CI, hiding a real regression.
RISK-3: Fuzz iterations are too few or not seeded, so a panic/data-loss path is missed or a failure cannot be reproduced.
RISK-4: Totality is under-checked — apply silently drops or duplicates a block on some conflict-resolution combination the totality assertion does not cover.
RISK-5: The suite quietly edits product code (src/**) to make a test pass, violating proof-only scope and masking a real MT-241 defect.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): a tripwire asserts document_diff_merge.ts exists at author time; captures are tagged from-TS-harness or hand-transcribed-with-reason; lifecycle.blocks=['MT-261'] enforces green-before-removal; no fabricated captures (GLOBAL-TRUTH).

CTRL-2 (RISK-2): every budget accepts a PROSE_PERF_BUDGET_*_MS override and the manifest records the MEASURED value + whether an override was applied, so a widened gate is visible, never hidden (MT-045 B1 precedent).
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): fuzz uses a seeded RNG (reproducible) over a substantial iteration count; the seed is recorded on failure.

CTRL-4 (RISK-4): totality asserts every changed block is classified exactly once AND apply's output block set equals the union of chosen sides for a complete resolution, across randomized complete resolutions.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): proof-only scope — grep/lineage proof that no src/** or backend file changed; a genuine MT-241 defect is reported back to MT-241, not patched here.
